chunks: There is no calamity that befalls the earth or your own selves but in accordance with the law (of causation) before We make it evident. This is indeed how the law of God works inevitably.

key_terms.أَنْ نَبْرَأَهَا: that We create it/make it evident
key_terms.إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ: except that it is in a book (divine record)
key_terms.وَلَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ: and in your own selves (internal/personal events)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine decree and calamities in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted to include both general natural occurrences and specific events befalling individuals, such as the trials of the Imams, underscoring that calamities are not random but part of a deliberate divine wisdom. The phrase 'prior to its creation' highlights the pre-eternal knowledge of Allah, reinforcing the concept of *Qadar* (divine decree) while allowing for human free will within that framework. This perspective encourages believers to view suffering as a means of spiritual purification and a sign of God's closeness rather than mere punishment.
